# Architecture for Line Counter (Go)

Project: `peerfoil-fixture-go` · Assurance: Guided · Revision: 1 · Status: accepted

- **Author:** architect (claude-code, anthropic-claude, session null)
- **Written at:** 2026-10-20T14:20:00Z
- **Decisions applied:** d-0001, d-0002, d-0003, d-0004
- **Quality Contract:** `.peerfoil/quality.md` revision 1
- **Reviews:** rv-0001

## Goals

A command-line program named linecount that prints the number of non-empty lines in a
text file. The user names the file as the single argument. A line counts when characters
remain after leading and trailing spaces and tabs are removed. A finished first phase
builds with the Go toolchain, passes its tests, and counts a real file correctly.

## Users

A single developer who runs the command in a terminal or a shell pipeline. The user needs
one number on standard output and a readable error on standard error when something goes
wrong. The user must not be exposed to stack traces or internal paths.

## Boundaries

Inside the project: one Go package with the command entry point, the counting logic, and
its tests. Outside the project: file creation, shells, and pipelines belong to the
operating system. The project relies on the Go toolchain for building, testing, and
static analysis instead of adding its own tooling.

## Dependencies

| Dependency | Purpose | License | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | The standard library covers file reading, string handling, and testing | — | Decision d-0004 keeps the project dependency-free |

## Data

The program reads the one text file the user names, assumes UTF-8 encoding, and writes a
single integer to standard output. It stores nothing, keeps no state between runs, and
sends nothing anywhere. There is no structured data, so grain and keys do not apply.

## Risks

| Risk | Response |
|---|---|
| Very large input files are read fully into memory | Accepted for the first phase; the files this user counts are small |
| Windows line endings leave a carriage return on each line, so a whitespace-only line may still count | Accepted for the first phase; the tests pin the counting rules for Unix line endings |

## Accessibility

The only user-facing surface is plain terminal text. Output and errors carry their
meaning in words and numbers, never in color alone, which satisfies the WCAG 2.2 Level AA
use-of-color requirement for this surface. The check is reading the output in a plain
terminal without color support.

## Security

The one trust boundary is the file path argument, which the operating system resolves;
the program passes it to the file-reading call unmodified and never to a shell. No
command, query, network call, or elevated permission exists. No action needs explicit
user approval beyond running the command.

## Privacy

No personal data. The program reads the file the user names and prints a count. Nothing
is logged, retained, or sent.

## Licensing

The project is the user's own code with no license declared yet. Decision d-0004 keeps
dependencies out, so no third-party notices apply. Copied material is not expected; if
any is added, it must carry its notice.

## Open decisions

d-0004 is assumed (Go 1.22, standard library only) and reversible. No decision is open.
